content.title: Management of diuretic therapy in acute heart failure (page excerpt)
content.summary: Guidance on initiation, dosing, monitoring and escalation of diuretic therapy in acute heart failure, including criteria for satisfactory diuretic response and considerations for transition to oral therapy.
content.initial_iv_dose_recommendation: Start with an initial IV dose of a loop diuretic (furosemide or equivalent bumetanide/torasemide) corresponding to 1–2 times the patient's usual daily oral dose prior to admission. If patient was not on oral diuretics, use a starting dose equivalent to ~20–40 mg IV furosemide (or bolus 10–20 mg IV torasemide).
content.administration_notes: Furosemide can be given as 2–3 daily boluses or as a continuous infusion; single daily boluses discouraged due to possible post-dosing sodium retention. Loading dose may be used with continuous infusion to reach steady state earlier.
content.assessment_and_monitoring: Evaluate diuretic response shortly after starting therapy by measuring spot urine sodium content at 2 or 6 hours and/or hourly urine output. Check serum creatinine and electrolytes at least every 24 hours when indicated.
content.satisfactory_diuretic_response_definitio: Urine sodium content ≥50–70 mEq/L at 2 h and/or urine output ≥100–150 mL/h during the first 6 h (values vary slightly across text: examples given 50–70 mEq/L and ≥100–150 mL/h).
content.insufficient_response_escalation: If response is insufficient, double the loop diuretic IV dose (e.g., double loop diuretic i.v. dose) with further reassessment. If hourly diuresis remains inadequate (<100 mL/h) despite doubling, consider concomitant administration of other diuretics acting at different sites (thiazides, metolazone, or acetazolamide) while carefully monitoring electrolytes and renal function.
content.dosing_algorithm_notes: Start with relatively low doses and frequently adjust based on early and frequent assessment to avoid dehydration and rises in serum creatinine; progressively decrease loop diuretic dose once significant negative fluid balance achieved.
content.transition_to_oral: Commence transition to oral treatment when the patient’s clinical condition is stable. After congestion relief, continue oral loop diuretics at the lowest effective dose to avoid recurrent congestion. Ensure adequate decongestion and an appropriate long-term diuretic dose before discharge to reduce risk of rehospitalization and death.
